rationale: Builds on the 9x512 recurrent-tail best by saving early training compute: the model trains with only the final recurrent tail block active until 58% of the usable train budget, then switches back to the full two-block tail for the later phase and final scored eval. The hypothesis is that the second recurrent pass is low-value while gates are near zero, so dropping it early can buy extra steps within 600s without changing the end architecture or quantized export path.
title: Single-Block Tail Recurrence Warmup
